digest.en: Lula secures a comeback victory over Flávio Bolsonaro in Brazil's runoff, shifting the balance of power in Latin America. Simultaneously, Vucic concedes defeat in Serbia, opening a window for renewed alignment with Western institutions. These twin electoral shifts reshape diplomatic calculations across two distinct regions.

articles.title: Full second round results as Lula wins comeback against Flávio Bolsonaro
articles.summary: Brazilian voters cast ballots on 25 October 2026 for the second round of the presidential election. Incumbent President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva faces Flávio Bolsonaro in a runoff. articles.title: Student-Led Opposition Celebrates In Serbia After Vucic Concedes Election Defeat
articles.summary: Aleksandar Vucic conceded defeat in Serbia's October 25 parliamentary elections. The student-led Students' List took a decisive lead in preliminary results. This ends his fourteen-year dominance of Serbian politics. Former President Aleksandar Vucic, who dominated Serbian politics for the past 14 years, conceded defeat in the country's parliamentary elections after polls closed on October 25. Preliminary results showed the movement called Students' List taking a decisive lead.

articles.title: Vucic Concedes Electoral Defeat, Setting Stage For New Era Of Serbian Politics, Relations With West
articles.summary: Vucic admitted defeat to the student-led protest movement in Serbia's parliamentary vote. His concession signals a potential shift toward European alignment. The new government may distance Serbia from Kremlin influence. Aleksandar Vucic, Serbia's former president and dominant political figure for more than a decade, conceded defeat to the student-led protest movement in the country's parliamentary elections, potentially ushering in a new era of politics more closely aligned with Europe and away from the Kremlin.

articles.title: Israeli air strikes kill several across Gaza Strip: local authorities

articles.title: Starlink back to 'the level ⁠we need' in Ukraine, Zelenskyy says

articles.title: Why ultra‑Orthodox parties will decide Netanyahu’s electoral fate
articles.summary: Israeli authorities detained dozens of Haredi men on 20 October 2026, a week before national elections. On October 20, 2026, a week before Israel’s elections, dozens of men were detained on suspicion of evading the draft – arrests that Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu called “unacceptable.” The young men attend ultra-Orthodox, or Haredi, religious schools, whose students were long exempt from the military service mandatory for most Israelis.

articles.summary: Russian officials face growing doubts about the Northern Sea Route's viability as a reliable trade corridor to China. articles.summary: Iran is repairing its Eagle 44 airbase in Hormozgan province after recent strikes. The subterranean facility demonstrates the value of hardened mountain shelters against precision firepower. This recovery offers a survival playbook for air forces facing superior adversaries. Iran’s rapid post-strike recovery of its Eagle 44 airbase proves that hardened mountain shelters remain a decisive shield against precision firepower, transforming how inferior air forces survive and deter superior adversaries.

articles.title: US-China AI race turning ASEAN neutrality into a liability
articles.summary: The U. S.-China AI competition is eroding ASEAN’s traditional neutrality. Southeast Asian nations previously leveraged ties with both powers for economic gain. Competing technology networks now force governments to choose sides, reducing their diplomatic flexibility and strategic room for maneuver. For decades, Southeast Asia has turned great-power rivalry to an economic advantage. By maintaining healthy ties with Washington and Beijing, ASEAN governments attracted investment, expanded trade and preserved room for diplomatic maneuver.

articles.title: ज्वालामुखी फटते ही राख के बादलों में चमकती है बिजली, आखिर क्या है इस खौफनाक नजारे का रहस्य?
articles.summary: ज्वालामुखी विस्फोट के दौरान राख के कण आपस में टकराकर विद्युत आवेश उत्पन्न करते हैं। अनुकूल परिस्थितियों में इन बादलों के भीतर बिजली चमकती है। इस प्राकृतिक घटना को डर्टी थंडरस्टॉर्म कहा जाता है, जहाँ राख और ज्वालामुखीय पदार्थ बादलों को घना बनाते हैं। ज्वालामुखी विस्फोट के दौरान राख और चट्टानों के छोटे-छोटे कण आपस में टकराते हैं. इससे विद्युत आवेश अलग-अलग हो सकते हैं और अनुकूल परिस्थितियों में बादलों के भीतर बिजली चमक सकती है.
